purpose: Check whether the H.264 segment containing the previously observed drop position has duplicate, reversed, or sub-millisecond video timestamps before and after hls.js remuxing.

scope.relationToDropRun: The earlier drop occurred at media time 950.070428 inside sequence 157. These bytes were regenerated later from the same fixture, sequence, KonomiTV commit, and encoding settings; they are not the retained bytes from the original drop run.
scope.diagnosticOnly: CDP response-body and SourceBuffer-input capture add overhead. Dropped-frame counts from the capture runs are excluded from performance comparisons.

video.codec: H.264 High level 4.2, yuv420p, coded 1440x1080, SAR 4:3

hlsJsVideoFmp4.stage: Video BUFFER_APPENDING data immediately before SourceBuffer append

result: The MPEG-TS video PTS sequence is strictly increasing and consists only of the 1501/1502 tick alternation required for 60000/1001 fps.
The hls.js fMP4 input to SourceBuffer preserves the same 440 frames, PTS values, interval histogram, and key-frame positions.
The known segment does not exercise Chromium's enqueue-drop paths for reversed timestamps, duplicate timestamps, or intervals below one millisecond.

This shifts the leading explanation for the observed drop toward a decoded frame missing its presentation deadline. It does not prove that every segment has clean timestamps or identify the Android decoder/compositor stage responsible.
